commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.description: Wheat is India's most important rabi food grain, covering over 30 million hectares and contributing 35% of national food grain output. Punjab and Haryana alone supply over 70% of wheat procured by FCI at MSP, making government procurement the dominant route for farmers in these states.
uses: Chakki atta for chapati & roti (primary use)
Semolina (sooji/rava) for sweets & upma
Maida for bread, biscuit & noodle factories
Wheat bran for cattle & poultry feed
Industrial starch and glucose syrup

commodities.name: Rice (Paddy)
commodities.description: Rice is the staple food for over 65% of India's population and the country's largest food grain crop by acreage. India is the world's largest rice exporter - Basmati from Punjab/Haryana and non-Basmati from West Bengal and AP earn over ₹40,000 crore in annual export revenue.
uses: Cooked rice - primary staple food
Poha (flattened rice) and chiwda snacks
Idli, dosa, appam batter (broken/parboiled)
Rice bran oil extraction
Straw for cattle feed and thatch roofing

commodities.name: Maize (Corn)
commodities.description: Maize is India's third-largest cereal and the fastest-growing staple, driven by surging demand from poultry feed (60% of domestic use), starch, ethanol and corn oil industries. Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are the leading producing states, with double-cropping increasingly common.
uses: Poultry and animal feed (60% of usage)
Starch, glucose and dextrose manufacturing
Corn oil production
Ethanol/biofuel blending
Makki ki roti and local food uses

commodities.name: Jowar (Sorghum)
commodities.description: Jowar (sorghum) is India's fourth-largest cereal and one of the most drought-tolerant staple crops, requiring 70% less water than rice. Maharashtra grows over 50% of India's rabi jowar and the grain commands premium prices in organic and health food markets due to its gluten-free, high-fibre profile.
uses: Jowar bhakri (roti) - staple in Maharashtra & Karnataka
Popped jowar snacks and health foods
Fodder and silage for cattle (high stover value)
Starch extraction for industrial use
Brewing and distillery industries

commodities.name: Bajra (Pearl Millet)
commodities.description: Bajra (pearl millet) is the most heat and drought-tolerant of India's major cereals, making it the crop of choice for Rajasthan's arid zones. India produces over 50% of global bajra and it is increasingly exported as a health grain to Europe and the USA, where it commands ₹40-60/kg in specialty stores.
uses: Bajra roti - staple winter food in Rajasthan/Haryana
Pearl millet flour for gluten-free health foods
Livestock and poultry feed
Fodder crop (bajra chara)
Export as health grain to Europe and North America

commodities.name: Barley
commodities.description: Barley is India's oldest cultivated cereal and the primary raw material for malt, beer and whisky manufacturing in India's ₹3 lakh crore alcobev industry. Rajasthan produces over 40% of India's barley, with malting-grade barley fetching a 25-30% premium over feed grade.
uses: Malting for beer and whisky (biggest industrial use)
Sattu (roasted flour) in Bihar/Rajasthan
Livestock and poultry feed
Jau ki roti and porridge
Pharmaceutical (beta-glucan health supplements)

commodities.name: Onion
commodities.description: Onion is India's most politically sensitive vegetable - price spikes above ₹80/kg have toppled state governments and triggered export bans. India is the world's second-largest onion producer and primary exporter to Southeast Asia, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, earning ₹4,000-6,000 crore in export revenue in good years.
uses: Fresh onion - universal cooking ingredient
Dehydrated onion flakes and powder export (USA, Europe)
Onion pickle and chutneys
Export to Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Malaysia
Onion seed production (high-value - ₹30,000-70,000/quintal)

commodities.name: Potato
commodities.description: Potato is India's most produced vegetable by tonnage with over 53 million tonnes annually, making India the world's second-largest producer. Agra and Kannauj in UP and Hooghly in West Bengal are the dominant trading hubs, and the chip-grade processing industry (PepsiCo, McCain, ITC) purchases 15-20% of potato production at contracted prices.
varieties: Kufri Sindhuri (red skin, long shelf life)
uses: Fresh table potato (dominant use)
Potato chips and French fries processing
Potato starch for textile, paper and food industry
Potato flour for health food products
Vodka and ethanol production (experimental)

commodities.name: Tomato
commodities.description: Tomato is India's highest-value vegetable crop in total market value and infamous for extreme price volatility - the same field can fetch ₹500/quintal in a glut and ₹8,000/quintal in a shortage within the same year. Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka together contribute 20% of national output; Kolar (Karnataka) and Madanapalle (AP) are India's primary tomato trading hubs.
uses: Fresh consumption and cooking (primary)
Tomato puree, paste and ketchup manufacturing
Dehydrated tomato flakes and powder export
Lycopene extraction (nutraceutical)
Canned whole tomatoes for export

commodities.name: Garlic
commodities.description: India is the world's second-largest garlic producer (after China) and Madhya Pradesh's Mandsaur district is the garlic capital of India where the entire regional economy revolves around this single crop. Indian garlic commands strong export prices in Malaysia, Sri Lanka and the UK due to its pungent flavour profile from high allicin content.
uses: Fresh garlic for household cooking
Garlic paste and dehydrated garlic powder export
Garlic pickle (lahsun ka achar)
Pharmaceutical - allicin supplements for cardiovascular health
Pest repellent spray for organic farming

commodities.name: Ginger
commodities.description: India is the world's largest producer and consumer of ginger, and Meghalaya's Tura ginger has a GI tag for its high gingerol content. The North-East (Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim) produces the finest quality dry ginger fetching premium prices from spice exporters in Kochi and Mumbai.
uses: Fresh ginger for household cooking and chai
Dry ginger (sonth) powder for spice blends
Ginger oil and oleoresin for flavour industry
Ginger extract for Ayurvedic medicines
Export of dry ginger to Japan, USA and Middle East

commodities.name: Chili (Mirch)
commodities.description: India is the world's largest producer, consumer and exporter of chillies (dry and fresh), with Andhra Pradesh's Guntur district the global hub - over 30% of world chilli trade passes through Guntur. Indian chillies command premium prices for their capsaicin content, natural colour and pungency, with exports to the USA, UK and Middle East exceeding ₹4,500 crore annually.
uses: Dry red chilli for spice blends (garam masala, curry powder)
Chilli powder and chilli flakes export
Capsaicin extraction for pharmaceuticals
Red food colouring (paprika oleoresin)
Pickles and sauces (hot sauce manufacture)

commodities.name: Cotton
commodities.description: India is the world's largest cotton producer and the second-largest exporter, with the cotton textile and apparel industry directly employing 45 million people. Bt cotton (Bollgard II) covers 95% of India's cotton area, but the pest resistance battle with pink bollworm is an ongoing challenge that can affect yields and quality sharply.
varieties: Bollgard II hybrids (most of India - 95% area)
uses: Cotton lint for textile spinning mills
Cotton seed oil - major industrial and edible oil
Cottonseed cake for dairy cattle feed
Cotton linters for paper and currency notes
Medical cotton (surgical cotton)

commodities.name: Sugarcane
commodities.season: Plant: Feb-Mar (spring) or Oct-Nov (autumn), Harvest: 10-12 months
commodities.description: Sugarcane is India's second-most important commercial crop and the raw material for India's 700+ sugar mills plus 350+ distilleries producing ethanol for fuel blending. Uttar Pradesh alone accounts for over 40% of national sugarcane area; the FRP (Fair and Remunerative Price) set by the government guarantees a floor price for all cane sold to mills.
uses: Raw and refined sugar production
Ethanol for fuel blending (20% blending target)
Jaggery (gur) and khandsari sugar
Bagasse for power generation (co-generation)
Molasses for distilleries and cattle feed

commodities.name: Jute
commodities.description: Jute is India's premier natural fibre crop and India is the world's largest jute producer (over 60% of global output). West Bengal contributes 80% of India's jute, and with rising global demand for biodegradable packaging as a substitute for plastic, jute prices have strengthened significantly after years of decline.
uses: Jute sacking and hessian bags for grain storage (government mandated)
Jute textiles and rugs for export
Biodegradable packaging replacing plastic
Jute geotextiles for soil erosion control
Paper and pulp from jute sticks

commodities.name: Soybean
commodities.description: Soybean is India's most important oilseed by value and the primary raw material for the ₹1 lakh crore edible oil and soy meal industry. Madhya Pradesh produces 50% of India's soybean and the crop directly feeds the poultry industry through soy meal, India's most-used poultry protein ingredient.
uses: Soy oil extraction (40% of Indian edible oil supply)
Soy meal/cake for poultry and fish feed
Soy flour and soy milk
Soy protein isolate for food manufacturing
Tofu, tempeh and soy-based health products

commodities.name: Mustard (Rapeseed)
commodities.description: Mustard is India's second-largest oilseed crop and the primary cooking oil in North and East India, with Rajasthan producing nearly 50% of national output. Indian mustard oil has zero trans-fat and high omega-3 content, driving export demand to the UK, US and Europe's Indian diaspora communities.
uses: Sarson tel (mustard oil) - primary cooking oil in North India
Mustard seeds for tempering (tadka)
Mustard paste (kasundi) and pickles
Mustard bran/deoiled cake for cattle feed
Lubricant and bio-diesel feedstock

commodities.name: Groundnut
commodities.description: Groundnut is India's largest oilseed by area and Gujarat produces the world-famous 'Saurashtra Bold' groundnut, which commands premium prices in the export confectionery market. India exports 5-7 lakh tonnes annually, primarily to Indonesia, Vietnam and Malaysia, earning over ₹8,000 crore in foreign exchange.
uses: Groundnut oil - major cooking oil in Gujarat and South India
Roasted groundnuts - domestic snack market
Groundnut butter (peanut butter) export
Groundnut cake for cattle and poultry feed
Confectionery ingredient (sweets, chikki)

commodities.name: Sunflower
commodities.description: Sunflower oil is India's second-most imported edible oil after palm oil, meaning domestic production consistently gets strong prices near MSP. Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh are the leading producers, and the crop's short 90-100 day duration makes it a profitable option in irrigated double-cropping systems.
uses: Sunflower oil - light cooking oil and salad oil
Sunflower seeds - health snack and birdseed
Sunflower cake for cattle and poultry feed
Sunflower heads for decorative floriculture
Bio-diesel feedstock (experimental in India)

commodities.name: Sesame (Til)
commodities.description: Sesame (til) is one of the world's oldest oilseed crops and India is the largest exporter, shipping to China, Japan, South Korea and the USA. Indian sesame - especially white sesame from Gujarat and West Bengal - commands ₹12,000-20,000/quintal in export markets, making it one of the highest-value oilseed crops per hectare.
uses: Til oil - traditional cooking and ayurvedic massage oil
Sesame seeds for tahini, hummus, bread topping
Tilgul (sesame-jaggery sweet) for festivals
Export to Japan (sushi topping) and Middle East
Sesame cake for cattle feed

commodities.name: Gram (Chana)
commodities.description: Gram (chana) is India's largest pulse crop by area and production, accounting for nearly 50% of total pulse output. Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are the dominant producers, and India's ₹15,000+ crore besan (gram flour) processing industry drives significant additional demand beyond the food grain market.
uses: Besan (chickpea flour) for pakoras, sweets, bread
Dalia and whole chana for curries
Chanajor garam and roasted chana snacks
Dal (split gram) for dals and soups
Animal feed from chana straw (bhoosa)

commodities.name: Arhar (Tur/Pigeon Pea)
commodities.description: Arhar (tur dal) is India's most consumed pulse and an essential protein source for 1.4 billion people. India imports 3-5 lakh tonnes annually from Myanmar, Australia and Canada to meet demand, making domestic production highly sensitive to import policy - import duty changes can swing mandi prices by ₹500-1000/quintal within days.
uses: Tur dal - India's most popular split pulse
Sambar base in South India
Papad and besan blending
Green pods as vegetable (sabji)
Crop residue for fuel and cattle feed

commodities.name: Moong (Green Gram)
commodities.description: Moong (green gram) is the fastest-maturing major pulse with a 60-75 day crop cycle, making it popular as a summer/zaid short-duration crop between two main kharif/rabi crops. Its high protein content (24%) and easy digestibility make it one of the fastest-growing health food ingredients in urban markets.
uses: Moong dal (split) for dals and soups
Sprouts (ankurit moong) - health food
Moong flour for chillas and papad
Green pods sold as a vegetable
Moong dal halwa and traditional sweets

commodities.name: Urad (Black Gram)
commodities.description: Urad (black gram) is the primary pulse for South Indian cuisine - every idli and dosa batter requires urad dal - making it one of the most price-sensitive pulses in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. India is both the world's largest producer and importer of urad, with Myanmar supplying 8-12 lakh tonnes annually.
uses: Urad dal (split) for dal tadka and soups
Idli and dosa batter - essential ingredient
Papad (urad papad) - large commercial use
Dal makhani (whole black urad)
Ayurvedic preparations for joint health

commodities.name: Masur (Lentil)
commodities.description: Masur (red lentil) is the most consumed pulse in eastern India and Bangladesh and India's cheapest source of dietary protein at ₹60-80/kg retail. Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh produce 80% of India's masur, and Canada/Australia compete directly in the Indian market, keeping domestic prices suppressed near MSP.
uses: Masur dal - everyday household dal
Split red lentil soup and stews
Masur dal flour for baby food
Papad blending ingredient
Imli masur (tamarind lentil) regional dishes

commodities.name: Turmeric
commodities.description: India produces 80% of the world's turmeric and is the largest exporter, primarily from Telangana's Nizamabad and Erode in Tamil Nadu (world's largest turmeric market). The curcumin content of Indian turmeric drives a global health supplement market worth ₹8,000 crore annually, with curcumin extract selling at ₹3,000-8,000/kg in international markets.
varieties: Lakadong Turmeric (Meghalaya GI - 7-12% curcumin, vs 2-4% normal)
uses: Turmeric powder - universal spice (haldi)
Curcumin extract for health supplements (export)
Natural yellow food colouring (E100)
Ayurvedic medicines and haldi doodh (golden milk)
Turmeric oil for cosmetics and anti-inflammatory creams

commodities.name: Coriander (Dhaniya)
commodities.description: India is the world's largest producer and consumer of coriander (dhania) and Rajasthan's Kota region accounts for 60% of national production. Both the dried seed (as spice) and the fresh leaves (as herb) are separately traded, with dried coriander export to Bangladesh, Malaysia and the USA earning ₹1,200-1,500 crore annually.
uses: Coriander powder - essential spice blend ingredient
Fresh coriander leaves (dhania patta) - garnish
Coriander seed export (whole and split)
Coriander seed oil for perfumery and flavouring
Digestive tea and Ayurvedic formulations

commodities.name: Cumin (Jeera)
commodities.description: India produces and exports 70% of the world's cumin (jeera) and Gujarat's Mehsana and Rajasthan's Barmer-Jalore belt are the world's most important cumin-growing regions. Unjha mandi in Gujarat is the world's single largest cumin spot market - Unjha prices set the global benchmark. Cumin is India's second-most valuable spice export after chilli, earning ₹5,000-8,000 crore annually.
uses: Jeera - universal tempering spice
Cumin powder for spice blends and masalas
Export to USA, Japan, Saudi Arabia
Cumin essential oil for perfumery and pharma
Digestive and flatulence medicine (Ayurveda)

commodities.name: Banana
commodities.description: India is the world's largest banana producer with over 31 million tonnes annually, and Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu together account for 40% of production. The Grand Naine variety (Cavendish type) dominates the fresh export market to the Middle East, while Nendran from Kerala and Poovan from Tamil Nadu command significant premium prices for their unique flavour and are processed into banana chips - a ₹3,000+ crore snack industry.
uses: Fresh eating (world's most consumed fruit)
Banana chips and wafers (Kerala cottage industry to national brand)
Export of fresh bananas to UAE and UK
Raw banana sabji and kofta
Baby food and weaning puree (first baby food globally)

commodities.name: Castor
commodities.description: Castor oil is a unique industrial oilseed with no edible substitute - its derivatives are used in over 700 industrial applications from aviation lubricants to biodegradable plastics. India controls 85-90% of global castor oil trade (₹6,000+ crore/year) and Gujarat's Saurashtra region is the undisputed global castor capital.
uses: Castor oil for lubricants and hydraulic fluids
Sebacic acid for nylon and plastics manufacturing
Cosmetics and pharmaceuticals (castor oil USP grade)
Biodiesel and bio-lubricants
Castor cake as fertiliser and fish pond conditioner

commodities.name: Brinjal
commodities.description: India is the world's second-largest brinjal producer with West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar growing the most - brinjal bharta and baingan masala are among India's most universally consumed vegetables. The crop grows year-round with multiple harvests and is one of the most reliable income sources for small vegetable farmers in eastern India.
uses: Baingan bharta and curry (universal Indian dish)
Stuffed brinjal (bharwa baingan)
Dehydrated brinjal chips (emerging snack)
Baby food ingredient
Ayurvedic use for diabetes management

commodities.name: Cauliflower
commodities.description: India is the world's second-largest cauliflower producer with West Bengal, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh dominating production. The crop is extremely price-sensitive to temperature - even a 2-3°C variation during curd development affects quality and can flood the market, causing prices to crash from ₹2,500 to ₹300/quintal within a week.
uses: Fresh vegetable for gobhi sabji and manchurian
Pickled cauliflower (gobi ka achar)
Frozen cauliflower export to Europe
Cauliflower rice (low-carb health substitute)
Dehydrated cauliflower for processed food

commodities.name: Cabbage
commodities.description: India is the world's third-largest cabbage producer and Odisha and West Bengal supply most of eastern India's requirement year-round. Cabbage is a high-yield, fast-maturing crop (60-90 days) that many small farmers use as an intercrop with potato, making it an important income-stabiliser in the rabi season.
uses: Fresh coleslaw and sabji (universal use)
Sauerkraut and kimchi fermentation
Cabbage soup and stew
Dehydrated cabbage for noodle seasoning
Juice for Ayurvedic ulcer treatment

commodities.name: Green Peas
commodities.description: Green peas are one of India's most widely cultivated winter vegetables and a versatile ingredient used in everything from matar paneer to samosa filling. Uttar Pradesh's Barabanki, Farrukhabad and Kannauj districts produce the best quality peas for fresh market, while Himachal Pradesh and Punjab supply the frozen pea processing industry.
uses: Fresh green peas for sabji and curries
Frozen peas processing (Bonduelle, Heritage)
Matar paneer and samosa filling
Matar pulao and biryani
Split pea dal and flour

commodities.name: Okra (Ladyfinger)
commodities.description: Okra (bhindi) is India's most widely grown vegetable crop with production spread across virtually every state. India is the world's second-largest producer and the crop is a key income earner for small farmers due to its high market frequency - it is picked every 2-3 days and sold fresh at local mandis, generating more transaction revenue per hectare than many other vegetables.
uses: Fresh bhindi sabji (most consumed green vegetable)
Stuffed bhindi (bharwa bhindi)
Okra soup (South India sambar)
Dehydrated okra flakes for export
Mucilage (okra slime) for paper and textile sizing

commodities.name: Cucumber
commodities.description: Cucumber is among India's top 10 most traded vegetables and is consumed fresh as a salad vegetable across all regions. The crop has two main growing seasons - summer (with irrigation) and kharif - and yields very quickly (40-50 days), making it a short-term cash crop for vegetable farmers during lean months.
uses: Fresh salad and raita
Pickled cucumber (kheera ka achar)
Cucumber juice and skin care (cosmetic industry)
Dehydrated cucumber powder
Cooling beverage ingredient (jal jeera drinks)

commodities.name: Carrot
commodities.description: India is the world's third-largest carrot producer and Haryana's Shahabad and Punjab's Hoshiarpur are the primary supply centres for North India's demand. The red Indian carrot (gajar) - deeper red and sweeter than European orange carrots - is used exclusively for the iconic gajar ka halwa winter dessert and commands a premium in the winter season.
uses: Fresh eating and gajar ka halwa (winter dessert)
Carrot juice and health drinks
Baby carrot processing for export
Dehydrated carrot flakes for instant food
Carrot seed oil for cosmetics and pharmaceuticals

commodities.name: Radish
commodities.description: Radish is India's fastest-maturing vegetable (25-30 days from sowing) and a staple winter crop for small farmers who grow it as a quick cash crop between main vegetables. The mooli of Patiala (Punjab) and Nasik (Maharashtra) are particularly prized; India also grows Asian giant radishes (daikon type) for the Korean kimchi export market.
uses: Fresh mooli and radish salads
Mooli paratha (Punjab winter staple)
Pickle (mooli ka achar)
Radish leaves (mooli ka saag)
Daikon export to South Korea and Japan for kimchi

commodities.name: Bottle Gourd
commodities.description: Bottle gourd (lauki/ghia/doodhi) is India's most widely cultivated summer gourd and one of the most affordable vegetables - its watery, easily digestible flesh makes it a year-round health food recommended for diabetics, weight management and post-illness recovery. UP and Bihar together account for nearly 50% of India's bottle gourd area.
uses: Lauki sabji and kofta (daily vegetable)
Lauki halwa and kheer (sweet)
Fresh juice for diabetes management
Dried lauki for murukku and sun-dried snacks
Lauki seed oil (cosmetic use)

commodities.name: Bitter Gourd
commodities.description: Bitter gourd (karela) is India's most medicinally important vegetable and commands a significant premium in the pharmaceutical and nutraceutical market - its bitter compounds (momordicin, charantin) are clinically studied for blood sugar management, driving exports to the UK, USA and Canada's South Asian diaspora at ₹150-300/kg retail.
uses: Karela sabji - daily blood-sugar management vegetable
Karela juice (health tonic market - large urban demand)
Bitter gourd extract capsules (nutraceutical export)
Dried karela powder for Ayurvedic medicines
Karela pickle export to South Asian diaspora

commodities.name: Pumpkin
commodities.description: Pumpkin is India's most productive cucurbit with yields of 20-30 tonnes/hectare and near-zero input requirements - it grows freely on any soil and waste water, making it an important food security crop in tribal and hill regions. The seed is a valuable byproduct with global export demand: pumpkin seeds sell at ₹150-250/kg in health food markets.
uses: Petha sweet (Agra petha - famous confection from ash gourd/kaddu)
Kaddu ki sabji (daily vegetable)
Pumpkin seed export to Germany and USA (health food)
Pumpkin seed oil (nutraceutical)
Livestock fodder from pumpkin vines

commodities.name: Spinach
commodities.description: Spinach is India's most nutritionally dense leafy vegetable and palak paneer is one of India's most ordered restaurant dishes, creating consistent demand throughout the winter season. India's baby spinach export to the UAE, UK and USA is growing at 15% annually, with Pune and Nasik supplying most of the export-grade produce.
uses: Palak paneer and palak dals (primary restaurant dish)
Fresh baby spinach salads and export
Palak paratha and smoothies
Spinach powder for food colouring (natural green)
Ayurvedic use for anaemia treatment (iron content)

commodities.name: Capsicum
commodities.description: Capsicum (shimla mirch) is India's highest-value open-field vegetable crop, with Karnataka's Hassan and Kolar districts and Maharashtra's Nasik commanding ₹4,000-8,000/quintal for premium coloured varieties exported to the UAE and UK. Polyhouse cultivation of red, yellow and orange capsicum in Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan earns ₹5-10 lakh/acre/year for progressive farmers.
uses: Fresh cooking vegetable (shimla mirch sabji)
Export of coloured capsicum to UAE and Europe
Pizza and salad topping
Pickled capsicum and chilli sauce
Paprika and capsicum oleoresin for food colouring

commodities.name: Green Chilli
commodities.description: Green chilli is the world's most consumed spice ingredient and India produces over 90% of its own requirement plus exports significant quantities to the South Asian diaspora globally. Andhra Pradesh's Warangal and Khammam districts are the primary green chilli trading hubs, with direct exports to the USA, UK and UAE.
uses: Fresh chilli for cooking across all Indian cuisines
Green chilli pickle (hari mirch ka achar)
Chilli sauce and sambal manufacturing
Export to South Asian diaspora markets
Capsaicin extraction for pain-relief creams

commodities.name: Sweet Potato
commodities.description: Sweet potato is Odisha's most important secondary food crop and a critical food security vegetable for tribal communities in eastern India who consume it as a staple during lean months. India's sweet potato industry is growing rapidly with rising awareness of its prebiotic fibre, beta-carotene and anthocyanin content in urban health food markets.
uses: Boiled and roasted sweet potato (tribal staple)
Shakarkandi chaat (winter street food)
Sweet potato flour for chips and snacks
Baby food and weaning cereals (natural sweetness)
Beta-carotene and starch extraction for food industry

commodities.name: Colocasia (Arbi)
commodities.description: Colocasia (arbi/taro) is one of India's oldest cultivated vegetables dating back 7,000 years and is a staple of coastal and tribal India. Kerala's chembu, UP's arbi and Maharashtra's alu are different regional variants with distinct taste profiles, and the corm, leaves and stem are all traded separately in local markets.
uses: Arbi/taro curry and dry sabji
Colocasia chips and fryums (popular snack)
Colocasia leaves (patra - Gujarat Jain dish)
Taro flour for health food
Ayurvedic use as a tonic vegetable

commodities.name: Drumstick (Moringa)
commodities.description: Drumstick (moringa) is the most nutritionally rich food tree in the world - the leaves contain 7× more vitamin C than oranges and 4× more calcium than milk - and India is both the world's largest moringa producer and exporter. Tamil Nadu's Dharmapuri and Karnataka's Bellary supply 80% of India's drumstick output, and moringa leaf powder export (₹600-1,200/kg) to USA, Europe and Japan is one of India's fastest-growing agri-exports.
uses: Fresh pods for sambar, curry and stir-fry
Moringa leaves as nutritious vegetable (sajna patta)
Moringa leaf powder export (superfood supplement)
Moringa seed oil (ben oil) for cosmetics
Moringa tea and health beverages

commodities.name: Beetroot
commodities.description: Beetroot is experiencing a surge in demand driven by urban health and fitness trends - beetroot shots, smoothies and nitrate supplements have made it a premium ingredient at ₹40-80/kg retail. Maharashtra and Karnataka produce most of India's beetroot, with the crop increasingly grown under protected cultivation for consistent supply to juice bars and health food companies.
uses: Beetroot halwa and salads (traditional use)
Cold-pressed beetroot juice (health/fitness)
Beetroot powder for natural red food colouring
Pickle and chutney
Dietary nitrate supplement for sports nutrition

commodities.name: French Beans
commodities.description: French beans are India's primary export vegetable, with Mahabaleshwar (Maharashtra), Ooty (Tamil Nadu) and Nainital (Uttarakhand) being the leading production centres that supply all-India hotels, restaurants and the UAE/UK export market. The crop is price-elastic - bumper production in Karnataka or Maharashtra can collapse prices to ₹500-800/quintal.
uses: Fresh vegetable for salads, stir-fry and curries
Frozen French beans export to UAE, Saudi Arabia, UK
Canned beans for retail
Bean salad and pasta mix ingredients
Dehydrated beans for instant soup mixes

commodities.name: Mango
commodities.description: India produces 45% of the world's mangoes and the fruit is India's national fruit, with over 1,000 named varieties. Alphonso (Hapus) from Ratnagiri gets ₹15,000-35,000/quintal while common varieties trade at ₹2,000-4,000/quintal, demonstrating the enormous quality premium. India exports 45,000-55,000 tonnes of mango annually to UAE, UK and Bangladesh.
uses: Fresh mango consumption (primary use)
Aamras and mango pulp export
Mango pickle (aam ka achar - India's largest pickle segment)
Aamchur (dried mango powder) for cooking
Mango juice, drinks and ice cream manufacturing

commodities.name: Grapes
commodities.description: Nashik in Maharashtra accounts for 80% of India's table grape production and is India's premier grape-growing region with a climate comparable to European wine regions. India exports 25,000-35,000 tonnes of seedless grapes (Thompson Seedless, Sonaka) to the Netherlands, UK and Russia annually, earning ₹500-700 crore in foreign exchange.
uses: Fresh table grapes (primary domestic use)
Seedless raisin (kishmish) drying
Export of fresh grapes to Europe and Russia
Grape juice and wine manufacturing (emerging)
Raisin export to Middle East

commodities.name: Pomegranate
commodities.description: India is the world's largest pomegranate producer and the Bhagwa variety from Solapur (Maharashtra) has become India's premium export pomegranate, fetching ₹12,000-20,000/quintal in Holland, Bangladesh and UAE markets. Maharashtra's Nashik-Solapur belt grows 80% of India's pomegranate and the crop's year-round income-generating potential makes it the most profitable orchard crop per hectare.
uses: Fresh arils for consumption and export
Pomegranate juice and cold-pressed juice export
Anardana (dried pomegranate seeds) for cooking
Pharmaceutical - punicic acid and antioxidant extract
Wine and fermented pomegranate drink

commodities.name: Apple
commodities.description: Jammu & Kashmir produces 75% of India's apple and the Himalayan apple industry is a ₹10,000+ crore economy supporting 3 million farming households. Himachal Pradesh's Shimla apple has a GI tag and a dedicated fan following in Punjab and Delhi for its sweet-tart taste; however, growing competition from cheaper imported Chinese and New Zealand apples is a persistent concern.
uses: Fresh eating (primary use)
Apple juice and cider manufacturing
Dried apple slices and chips for export
Apple-based nutraceutical extracts
Mahua/apple wine (HP cottage industry)

commodities.name: Orange
commodities.description: Nagpur orange from Maharashtra has a prestigious GI tag as one of the world's best mandarin oranges - its distinctive seedless, juicy character drives premium retail pricing of ₹80-150/kg in metro markets. Maharashtra's Vidarbha region (Nagpur, Amravati, Wardha) and Assam's Meghalaya border districts are the primary producing zones.
uses: Fresh eating and gifting (primary use)
Orange juice and squash manufacturing
Nagpur orange export to UAE and UK
Orange peel oil for perfumery and food flavouring
Marmalade and candied peel export

commodities.name: Guava
commodities.description: Allahabad Safeda and Lucknow-49 guavas from Uttar Pradesh are India's most famous varieties, with the Allahabad Safeda holding a GI tag and commanding ₹50-100/kg retail. India is the world's largest guava producer and the fruit's extremely high vitamin C content (228 mg/100g - 4× orange) drives consistent demand from juice and vitamin-C supplement manufacturers.
varieties: Allahabad Safeda (GI tag - classic white flesh)
uses: Fresh eating and juice extraction
Guava paste and jelly (goiabada) for export
Vitamin C supplement manufacturing
Dehydrated guava powder for food fortification
Guava cheese (amrood ki barfi)

commodities.name: Papaya
commodities.description: India is the world's largest papaya producer with 5+ million tonnes annually, and Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh have become the dominant commercial producers of hybrid papaya. Papain enzyme extracted from raw papaya is a significant industrial product used in meat tenderisers, brewery clarification and pharmaceutical digestive enzymes, fetching ₹1,500-3,000/kg.
uses: Fresh eating and fruit salads
Raw papaya curry and salad (North-East India)
Papain enzyme extraction (industrial and pharmaceutical)
Papaya jam, juice and nectar
Beauty and skin care - papain-based face packs

commodities.name: Watermelon
commodities.description: India is the world's third-largest watermelon producer and the crop is a critical summer cash crop for farmers in the sandy riverbeds of UP, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, where it is grown on oozing sandy soil alongside river banks. Yellowing and tri-colour flesh varieties command 30-50% higher prices in urban markets and are a growing trend among commercial growers.
uses: Fresh eating (primary - summer cooling fruit)
Watermelon juice and sherbet
Watermelon seed (magaz) as a snack and Ayurvedic medicine
Watermelon rind curry (North India waste-free cooking)
Watermelon seed oil (cosmetic use)

commodities.name: Muskmelon
commodities.description: Muskmelon (kharbooja) is among India's most fragrant summer fruits and a traditional heat-quenching fruit in Rajasthan and UP. India grows both the orange-fleshed 'Pusa Madhuras' type and green-fleshed 'Durgapura' type, and the seeds (magaj) are traded as a separate premium commodity used in Mughal-origin creamy gravies and Unani medicine.
uses: Fresh eating and juice (summer cooling fruit)
Muskmelon seeds (magaj/chharmagaz) for Mughal gravies
Seed oil extraction for Unani medicines
Dehydrated muskmelon powder for health drinks
Traditional cooling drinks (thandai ingredient)

commodities.name: Pineapple
commodities.description: India's pineapple belt spans West Bengal, Assam, Tripura and Kerala, and the North-East produces 90% of India's pineapple. Assam's Kew variety and West Bengal's Queen variety are prized for sweetness, while the state of Tripura has built India's first pineapple-based wine and vinegar industry. Mega Food Parks in North-East India are driving pineapple processing (juice, pulp, candy) as a way to prevent post-harvest losses.
uses: Fresh eating and juice
Pineapple canning for export
Pineapple vinegar and wine (Tripura cottage industry)
Pineapple leaves for 'piña' textile fibre
Bromelain enzyme extraction (pharmaceutical use)

commodities.name: Litchi
commodities.description: Bihar's Muzaffarpur is the global capital of the Shahi litchi, which has a GI tag and is prized in the Middle East and Europe for its unique floral-sweet flavour profile. India exports 3,000-5,000 tonnes of fresh litchi annually at ₹300-500/kg retail, making it one of India's premium fruit exports despite a very narrow 3-4 week harvest window.
uses: Fresh eating (narrow May-Jun window)
Litchi juice and squash manufacturing
Canned litchi in syrup for export
Dried litchi (longan-style) for export
Litchi wine and vinegar (West Bengal micro-industry)

commodities.name: Sapota (Chiku)
commodities.description: Sapota (chiku) is India's 5th-largest fruit crop and nearly 70% of India's production comes from Gujarat's Anand, Valsad and Navsari districts. The fruit has one of the highest natural sugar contents among Indian fruits (14-20°Brix) and is a primary ingredient in sapota ice cream and sapota-flavoured milk drinks manufactured across Gujarat and Maharashtra.
uses: Fresh eating (very sweet, dessert fruit)
Sapota pulp for ice cream and milkshakes
Dried chiku slices for export to UK and Canada
Seed oil for edible and industrial use
Bark extract for traditional fever treatment

commodities.name: Coconut
commodities.description: India is the world's third-largest coconut producer and Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka together account for 90% of production. Coconut is a 'kalpavriksha' (wish-fulfilling tree) because every part is commercially traded: water, oil, shell, husk, toddy, coir fibre - making it India's most versatile plantation crop with 10-15 different revenue streams per tree.
uses: Coconut oil (hair and cooking oil)
Copra for edible oil extraction
Coconut water (packaged beverage industry)
Coir fibre for rope, mat and geotextile
Coconut shell charcoal and activated carbon

commodities.name: Lemon
commodities.description: India is the world's second-largest lemon and lime producer and the Kagzi lime (thin-skinned, high-juice variety) from Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan is the most valued commercial type. Lemon prices are extremely volatile - they can range from ₹1,500 to ₹8,000/quintal within the same year depending on whether summer demand spikes coincide with the lean harvest period.
uses: Fresh lemon in cooking and beverages
Lemon juice concentrate for beverages
Citric acid extraction for food industry
Lemon essential oil for perfumery and cosmetics
Pickle and preserved lemon export to Middle East

commodities.name: Fenugreek (Methi)
commodities.description: India is the world's largest methi producer and Rajasthan alone accounts for 80% of India's fenugreek cultivation, with Sikar and Nagaur being the key production districts. Fenugreek seeds contain diosgenin - a precursor for steroidal drugs - making it a pharmaceutical crop increasingly grown on contract for hormone and anti-diabetic drug manufacturing.
varieties: Kasuri Methi (Punjab - small leaf premium type)
uses: Methi powder for spice blends and curries
Fresh methi leaves (saag) - vegetable
Kasuri methi (dried leaves) - premium garnish spice
Diosgenin extraction for steroidal drug manufacturing
Galactagogue supplement for nursing mothers

commodities.name: Fennel (Saunf)
commodities.description: Gujarat's Unjha is the world's largest saunf (fennel) market, trading both as a mouth freshener after meals and as a primary spice. India's saunf candy and fennel-based digestive products are a ₹2,000+ crore market, and export of raw fennel seed to the USA, Malaysia and the UAE earns significant foreign exchange.
uses: Saunf mouth freshener after meals
Fennel powder for spice blends (sauf)
Fennel tea for digestion and infant colic
Essential oil (anethole) for flavouring and pharma
Candy and mukhwas (digestive sweet) manufacturing

commodities.name: Ajwain (Carom)
commodities.description: Ajwain (carom seeds) is India's most pungent spice and has virtually no global competition - India produces 90% of the world's ajwain. The seed's thymol content is extracted as a pharmaceutical ingredient used in antiseptic preparations, cough drops and oral hygiene products globally.
uses: Carom seeds for tempering puri, paratha and pickle
Ajwain water (omwala pani) as digestive remedy
Thymol extraction for pharmaceutical antiseptics
Cough and bronchitis medicine (Ayurveda)
Insect repellent (thymol vapour)

commodities.name: Black Pepper
commodities.description: India's Malabar black pepper was the original 'Black Gold' that drove European exploration of India and the spice trade. Kerala's Idukki district produces the finest quality pepper with 6-9% piperine content. India is the world's 3rd-largest producer but the 1st-largest consumer, relying on Vietnamese and Indonesian imports to meet domestic demand.
uses: Black pepper powder - universal spice
White pepper (peeled black pepper) for export
Piperine extraction for pharmaceutical bioavailability enhancers
Pepper oil for perfumery and flavouring
Pickled green peppercorns (gourmet export)

commodities.name: Cardamom
commodities.description: India's small cardamom (Elettaria cardamomum) from Kerala's Cardamom Hills has a GI tag and is traded at Bodinayakanur (Tamil Nadu) - Asia's largest cardamom auction. Indian cardamom commands premium prices from the Middle East (Gulf countries use it in qahwa/Arabic coffee) and contributes ₹3,000-4,000 crore in annual export earnings despite competition from Guatemalan cardamom.
uses: Elaichi - universal Indian dessert and chai spice
Arabic coffee (qahwa) flavouring - Gulf export
Cardamom oil for perfumery and pharmaceutical flavouring
Ayurvedic digestive and respiratory formulations
Elaichi-flavoured tobacco and paan

commodities.name: Clove
commodities.description: Indian clove, grown in Kerala and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, commands ₹900-1,300/kg wholesale - among the highest-priced spices in the world per kg. India imports significant quantities from Indonesia (world's largest producer) to meet domestic demand, and eugenol extracted from clove oil is the primary dental anaesthetic ingredient used globally in dentistry.
uses: Clove powder for garam masala and biryani
Eugenol extraction for dental anaesthetic
Clove oil for toothache and oral hygiene products
Cigarette flavouring (kretek clove cigarettes)
Clove in pickles, mulled wine and chai

commodities.name: Nutmeg (Jaiphal)
commodities.description: Kerala produces 95% of India's nutmeg and the mace (outer covering of the nutmeg seed) is often more valuable than the nut itself, fetching ₹80,000-1,50,000/quintal. Both nutmeg and mace are primarily exported to the USA, Netherlands and Singapore for pharmaceutical, food flavouring and perfumery industries.
uses: Nutmeg powder for garam masala and desserts
Mace (javitri) for biryanis and meat dishes
Nutmeg essential oil for pharmaceuticals and perfumery
Myristicin extraction (industrial)
Nutmeg butter (cocoa butter substitute for confectionery)

commodities.name: Tamarind
commodities.description: India is the world's largest tamarind producer with Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka together supplying global demand. Tamarind is the souring agent in virtually every South Indian dish (sambar, rasam, chutneys) and tamarind concentrate is a significant food-processing export, with the global tamarind products market valued at over ₹5,000 crore annually.
uses: Imli (tamarind) for South Indian cooking (sambar, rasam, chutneys)
Tamarind concentrate and paste export
Sweet-sour candy and tamarind toffee
Tamarind pulp for sauces and marinades
Xylose extraction from tamarind seed kernel (pharmaceutical and food)

commodities.name: Dry Ginger (Sonth)
commodities.description: Dry ginger (sonth) commands 3-5× the price of fresh ginger per kg due to its more intense gingerol and shogaol content and longer shelf life. Kerala's Wayanad and Meghalaya's Ri Bhoi district produce premium dry ginger exported to Japan and the USA for pharmaceutical-grade ginger extracts used in nausea treatment and anti-inflammatory supplements.
varieties: Kerala local (dried from Nadia or Maran fresh types)
uses: Sonth powder for masalas and Ayurvedic formulations
Ginger extract for pharmaceutical anti-nausea drugs
Ginger oil and oleoresin for food flavouring industry
Export to Japan, USA for nutraceuticals
Dry ginger tea for respiratory ailments

commodities.name: Cowpea (Lobia)
commodities.description: Cowpea (lobia) is one of India's most drought-tolerant and nitrogen-fixing legumes, capable of thriving in poor sandy soils of Rajasthan and Gujarat where other pulses fail. Both the dry seed and the green pods (as a vegetable) are commercially traded, and the leaves are an important leafy vegetable in tribal regions.
uses: Lobia dal and curries
Green pods as a vegetable (sabji)
Leaves as a leafy vegetable in tribal areas
Green fodder and silage for cattle
Nitrogen fixation (soil improvement as green manure)

commodities.name: Horse Gram (Kulthi)
commodities.description: Horse gram is the most protein-rich dryland pulse at 22-25% protein content and has been cultivated in India for over 4,000 years. It is the primary pulse crop of tribal farmers in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha grown on marginal lands without irrigation, and rising demand from Ayurvedic kidney-stone treatment products is pushing prices higher.
uses: Kulthi dal for traditional curries (horse gram rasam)
Ayurvedic medicine for kidney stones and urinary disorders
Horse feed and livestock supplement
Green manure and soil improvement
Sprouted kulthi as a health food

commodities.name: Dry Peas (Matar)
commodities.description: Dry field peas are a key rabi pulse of Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar, growing in the same season as wheat and requiring minimal irrigation. The processing industry converts dry peas into matar dal, matar flour for namkeen snacks, and pea protein isolate for plant-based food manufacturing.
uses: Matar dal (split yellow pea) for everyday cooking
Matar namkeen snacks (matar ki bhujiya)
Pea flour for pakoras and savoury snacks
Plant-based protein isolate manufacturing
Green pea processing (canning and freezing)

commodities.name: Rajma (Kidney Bean)
commodities.season: Kharif (Sow: Jun-Jul, Harvest: Oct-Nov); Rabi in hills
commodities.description: Rajma (kidney bean) is a premium pulse commanding ₹80-130/kg retail and is an essential ingredient in Punjabi cuisine's iconic rajma-chawal dish consumed across north India. India's best rajma comes from Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh hill farms, with Chitra rajma (speckled variety) from Kullu-Manali fetching the highest prices.
uses: Rajma-chawal - north India's most popular one-dish meal
Rajma curry and gravies
Kidney bean salads (health food)
Canned kidney beans for export
Animal feed from dried haulm (plant residue)

commodities.name: Linseed (Alsi)
commodities.description: Linseed (flaxseed) is a dual-purpose crop where the seed is pressed for oil used in paints and varnishes (linseed oil dries and polymerises - invaluable for wood preservation and artist oil paints) while the milled seed is a high-omega-3 health food. India's linseed export market is growing rapidly with rising global demand for omega-3 health supplements.
uses: Linseed oil for paints, varnishes and wood preservative
Flaxseed meal as high-omega-3 health supplement
Cattle feed (flaxseed cake boosts milk fat)
Linen fibre from flax stalks (Assam handloom)
Alsi ladoo and chutney in Madhya Pradesh

commodities.name: Niger Seed
commodities.description: Niger seed (ramtil) is India's exclusive tribal oilseed crop, grown almost entirely by adivasi communities in Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh on marginal rainfed land without any fertilisers. Its oil has a distinctive nutty flavour used in traditional cooking and the seed is a premium birdseed ingredient exported to the USA and Europe at ₹80-120/kg.
uses: Niger oil for traditional cooking in tribal areas
Premium birdseed export to USA and Europe
Ramtil chutney (local food use in Odisha)
Hair oil in tribal communities
Crop residue for cattle feed

commodities.name: Safflower (Kusum)
commodities.description: Safflower is a dual-purpose oilseed with both a high-oleic oil (better for frying than sunflower oil) and a dye industry using the red and yellow petals for natural fabric colouring. Maharashtra is the dominant producer but cultivation is declining as imported oils undercut it; the crop survives primarily due to MSP procurement.
uses: Safflower oil for cooking and salad oil
Natural dye (keshar substitute) from petals
Safflower tea and herbal health products
Carthamin natural food colourant for export
Safflower cake for cattle and poultry feed

commodities.name: Ragi (Finger Millet)
commodities.description: Ragi (finger millet) has the highest calcium content of any cereal (344 mg/100g) and is a nutritional powerhouse increasingly popular in health food markets. Karnataka grows 60% of India's ragi, and ragi-based processed products (cookies, malt, noodles) now sell for ₹80-200/kg in urban retail - 20× the farm gate price.
uses: Ragi mudde and roti - staple in Karnataka
Ragi malt (porridge) for infants and elders
Health food products: cookies, noodles, bread
Ragi malt flour (₹150-200/kg retail)
Animal feed and poultry ingredient

commodities.name: Foxtail Millet (Kangni)
commodities.description: Foxtail millet is one of India's oldest cultivated crops and a key component of India's Shree Anna (nutri-cereal) mission promoting millets globally. With a 45-day crop cycle, it is one of the fastest-maturing cereals and ideal for short-duration intercropping in dryland farming systems of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
uses: Cooked like rice as a staple grain
Foxtail millet flour for health breads and cookies
Baby food and weaning food formulations
Poultry and small livestock feed
Export as health grain (Shree Anna)

commodities.name: Kodo Millet
commodities.description: Kodo millet is a drought-tolerant tribal food crop of central India, especially Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, where it is grown on marginal soils without irrigation or chemical inputs. It is gaining commercial importance as a certified organic grain exported to health markets in Europe and Japan.
uses: Kodo rice (cooked grain) - tribal staple food
Kodo flour for rotis and porridge
Organic health food export to Europe and Japan
Poultry and small animal feed
Fermented drink (mahuli) in tribal communities

commodities.name: Little Millet (Kutki)
commodities.description: Little millet is the most versatile minor millet, suited to both rainfed uplands and waterlogged conditions, and is a dietary staple for tribal communities in Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Its rapid 75-day crop cycle and zero-input organic certification potential make it attractive for small and marginal farmers.
uses: Cooked little millet as a rice substitute
Little millet flour for health rotis
Organic certified export
Bird feed and small animal fodder
Traditional beer (hadia) in Jharkhand and Odisha

commodities.name: Sorghum Fodder
commodities.description: Sorghum fodder is the highest-yielding green fodder crop in India's arid and semi-arid zones, providing 40-60 tonnes/hectare of green biomass per year with 3-4 cuttings. It is the backbone of dairy farming in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra and commands steady prices from dairies and livestock farmers throughout the year.
uses: Green fodder for dairy cattle (primary use)
Silage making for dry-season feed reserves
Hay and dry fodder (chara)
Seed grain for poultry feed
Bio-ethanol feedstock (emerging)

commodities.name: Arecanut (Supari)
commodities.description: Arecanut (supari) is India's most cash-intensive plantation crop per unit area, with Karnataka's Shimoga district earning ₹3-5 lakh/acre/year for growers. Chewing betel nut is deeply embedded in Indian culture and the ₹60,000+ crore branded pan masala industry ensures perennial high demand despite health advisories.
uses: Fresh/tender supari for direct consumption
Dried and processed supari for pan and paan masala
Supari in puja/religious rituals
Betel nut extract for pharmaceutical preparations
Arecanut husk for particle board and mulching

commodities.name: Cashew Nut
commodities.description: India is the world's largest cashew processor, importing raw cashew nuts (RCN) from Africa and re-exporting processed kernels earning over ₹7,000 crore annually. Goa and Kerala cashews have GI tags and command premium prices, while Maharashtra's Sindhudurg district and Odisha are growing processing hubs.
uses: Processed cashew kernels for export and domestic snacking
Cashew apple juice (feni in Goa)
Cashew feni - Goa's famous spirit (GI product)
Cashew nut shell liquid (CNSL) - industrial chemical
Cashew cake for cattle feed

commodities.name: Natural Rubber
commodities.description: Natural rubber from India's Kerala plantations is prized in global tyre and industrial rubber markets for its superior quality. India is the world's 4th-largest rubber producer and consumer - the entire production is consumed domestically by the automotive tyre industry, making India a net importer despite significant production.
uses: Automotive tyres (60% of rubber use)
Latex gloves and medical rubber products
Industrial rubber products (belts, hoses)
Foam and mattresses
Adhesives and sealants

commodities.name: Tea (Green Leaf)
commodities.description: Assam tea has a GI (Geographical Indication) tag and is among the world's most recognised tea origins - its malty, robust character powers India's iconic 'cutting chai' culture. India is the world's second-largest tea producer and consumer, with over 1.3 billion kg consumed domestically, making India a net importer of certain grades despite massive production.
uses: CTC tea (crush-tear-curl) for mass-market chai
Orthodox loose leaf for premium export
Green tea for health market
Tea extract for RTD (ready-to-drink) beverages
Tea waste as compost and cattle feed supplement

commodities.name: Coffee
commodities.description: Karnataka's Coorg (Kodagu) and Chikkamagaluru districts produce 70% of India's coffee and are home to the world-famous Monsooned Malabar - a unique Indian coffee deliberately exposed to monsoon winds, creating a distinct earthy flavour prized by European specialty roasters at €10-20/kg. India exports 70-75% of its coffee production.
uses: Filter coffee for Indian domestic market
Specialty and single-origin export (Monsooned Malabar)
Instant coffee powder manufacturing
Green coffee beans for direct export
Coffee husk as fuel and organic fertiliser

commodities.name: Tobacco
commodities.season: Rabi (Sow: Sep-Oct, Transplant: Nov-Dec, Harvest: Feb-Apr)
commodities.description: India is the world's third-largest tobacco producer and second-largest exporter, earning ₹5,000-6,000 crore annually from tobacco leaf exports to Belgium, Germany and Russia. Andhra Pradesh's Guntur district produces 'flue-cured Virginia' (FCV) tobacco that sets global benchmark prices at the Guntur auction platform - Asia's largest tobacco auction.
uses: Cigarettes and bidis (primary use)
Chewing tobacco and gutkha
Hookah tobacco (shisha)
Snuff and smokeless tobacco products
Tobacco leaf export (raw leaf to Belgium, Germany)

commodities.name: Isabgol (Psyllium)
commodities.description: India produces and exports 85% of the world's isabgol (psyllium husk) - one of India's most dominant global agri-exports. Rajasthan's Jalor, Barmer and Pali districts are the world's isabgol capital. The pharmaceutical-grade husk is exported to the USA, Germany and UK as a bulk laxative and cholesterol-lowering supplement at ₹500-800/kg, making it India's highest-value oilseed-equivalent crop.
uses: Psyllium husk supplement (Metamucil, Sat Isabgol)
Cholesterol-lowering pharmaceutical (FDA-approved health claim)
Binding agent in tablet manufacturing
Food-grade thickener and stabiliser
Export to USA, Germany, UK in bulk

commodities.name: Onion Seed
commodities.description: Onion seed (kanda beej) is one of India's highest-value agricultural commodities - a single kg of hybrid onion seed can cost ₹3,000-5,000 and represents the most important input cost in onion cultivation. Maharashtra's Nashik and Gujarat's Bhavnagar are the primary onion seed production centres, with farmers dedicating specific plots to mother plants for seed harvest.
uses: Planting material for onion cultivation
Export of onion seeds to Bangladesh, Malaysia, Myanmar
Foundation and certified seed production
Hybrid seed production for seed companies
Onion seed oil (minor cosmetic use)

commodities.name: Ridge Gourd (Turai)
commodities.description: Ridge gourd (turai) is a staple summer vegetable of eastern India - West Bengal alone accounts for 35% of national production - and the dry loofah (sponge) made from its fibrous skeleton is a significant cottage industry export product. The crop is a reliable income earner for small farmers in Bihar and UP because it matures in 50-55 days and produces continuously for 60-70 days.
uses: Fresh vegetable (turai ki sabji)
Ridge gourd chutney (South India)
Loofah sponge for bathing (dry fibre export to Europe)
Ayurvedic use for skin conditions
Juice for liver health in Ayurveda

commodities.name: Pointed Gourd (Parwal)
commodities.description: Pointed gourd (parwal) is one of the most expensive vegetables in North India, commanding ₹40-80/kg retail in Delhi and UP during peak season, and is the only Cucurbit grown from vegetative cuttings rather than seeds. It is deeply embedded in Bengali and Odia cuisine and the 'parwal ki mithai' (pointed gourd sweet) is a signature Bengal festival delicacy.
uses: Parwal ki sabji and curry (North-East staple)
Parwal ki mithai - Bengali sweet (unique dessert)
Stuffed parwal (bharwa parwal)
Dried parwal for off-season use
Ayurvedic use for fever and diabetes management

commodities.name: Round Gourd (Tinda)
commodities.description: Round gourd (tinda) is a quintessential summer vegetable of North India - particularly Punjab, Haryana and UP - consumed daily during peak summer months when it provides hydration and heat relief. It is rarely found outside North India's markets despite being one of the most productive cucurbits, with 3-4 fruits per plant daily during the peak harvest period.
uses: Tinda sabji (North India summer staple)
Stuffed tinda (bharwa tinda)
Tinda raita (cooling summer dish)
Dehydrated tinda for off-season (local)
Traditional remedy for stomach cooling

commodities.name: Ash Gourd (Petha)
commodities.description: Ash gourd (petha/safed kaddu) is the raw material for Agra's world-famous petha sweet - a ₹500+ crore confectionery industry using over 5 lakh tonnes of ash gourd annually. The vegetable is also deeply revered in Vastu Shastra and religious traditions, commanding premium prices during festivals and temple festivals across India.
uses: Agra petha sweet manufacturing (₹500 crore industry)
Ash gourd halwa and sabji
Juice for Ayurvedic detox and mental health (vallarai juice)
Seeds as dry fruit snack (roasted)
Vastu/religious crop for doorways (protection belief)

commodities.name: Elephant Yam (Suran)
commodities.description: Elephant yam (suran/jimikand) is the most starchy tropical tuber crop of India and a primary food security crop in eastern India's tribal and rural communities. Odisha's Koraput region grows the finest quality suran with the highest dry matter content, and suran chips and dehydrated suran are emerging export products for health food markets in Japan and Europe.
uses: Suran sabji and curry (eastern India staple)
Suran chips and crisps (health snack)
Dehydrated suran powder for export
Ayurvedic medicine for piles treatment (a prescribed vegetable)
Sweets and halwa from suran (Maharashtra)

commodities.name: Ivy Gourd (Tindora)
commodities.description: Ivy gourd (tindora/kundru) is a perennial climbing cucurbit that, once established, produces prolifically for 10-12 years from a single planting - making it one of the most cost-effective vegetables for small farmers. Gujarat's Surat and Anand districts are the main commercial production centres and the vegetable is increasingly marketed for its blood-sugar-lowering properties.
uses: Tindora sabji (Gujarat, Maharashtra daily vegetable)
Stuffed tindora (bharwa kundru)
Blood sugar management - Ayurvedic prescription vegetable
Pickle and sun-dried tindora (achaar)
Perennial fence/boundary crop (dual agricultural use)

commodities.name: Sponge Gourd (Ghia Tori)
commodities.description: Sponge gourd (ghia tori/dodka) is extensively grown across humid eastern and western India and its fibrous interior - dried and sold as a natural loofah sponge - is a growing export product replacing synthetic bath sponges in eco-conscious European and US markets. The global natural loofah market is expanding at 8-10% annually.
varieties: Local WB selection (fibrous type for loofah)
uses: Fresh vegetable for turai-like curries
Natural loofah sponge production (export to EU/USA)
Loofah mats and bathroom accessories
Seeds as oil and food ingredient
Ayurvedic topical application for skin

commodities.name: Cluster Beans (Guar Phali)
commodities.description: Cluster bean (guar phali) vegetable and guar seed are two distinct markets - the fresh green pod is a vegetable while the dry seed (guar) is a globally strategic industrial crop because guar gum is the primary fracking fluid thickener used in the US and Canadian oil and gas industry. Rajasthan produces 80% of India's guar, making it a crop with both rural food security and global industrial significance.
uses: Fresh cluster beans sabji (vegetable use)
Guar gum for food thickener (E412 - ice cream, sauce)
Guar gum for oil drilling fracking fluid (industrial)
Guar protein meal for animal feed
Guar gum for textile sizing and paper manufacturing

commodities.name: Amaranthus (Chaulai)
commodities.description: Amaranthus (chaulai) is a dual-purpose crop - the green leaves are a nutritious leafy vegetable while the grain type (rajgira) is a gluten-free superfood with the highest protein content of any grain cereal (14-18%). Maharashtra's nashik and UP grow most of India's grain amaranth, which sells at ₹150-400/kg retail in health food markets.
uses: Chaulai saag (leafy vegetable)
Rajgira ladoo (festival sweet, Navratri fasting food)
Rajgira flour for gluten-free health products
Amaranth grain for protein bars and cereals
Natural red dye from amaranth pigment

commodities.name: Tapioca (Cassava)
commodities.description: India is one of the world's largest tapioca producers and Kerala and Tamil Nadu are the dominant growing states, where cassava (tapioca) is a primary food security crop. India is also the world's second-largest producer of tapioca starch - an industrial raw material for glucose syrups, monosodium glutamate (MSG), textile sizing, paper and biodegradable plastic manufacturing.
uses: Tapioca chips (kappa chips - Kerala snack)
Kappa (boiled tapioca with coconut chutney - Kerala staple)
Industrial tapioca starch for glucose, MSG, textiles
Sabudana (sago pearls from tapioca starch)
Bio-degradable plastic and ethanol production

commodities.name: Snake Gourd (Chichinda)
commodities.description: Snake gourd (chichinda) is a distinctive tropical vegetable growing up to 150 cm in length and is particularly popular in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala, where it is a primary rainy-season vegetable. Its watery, bitter-free flesh makes it one of the most cooling and digestible vegetables - widely prescribed in Ayurveda for heat-related ailments.
uses: Snake gourd sabji (South India daily vegetable)
Stuffed snake gourd (bharwa chichinda, Andhra style)
Snake gourd chutney (Kerala)
Ayurvedic fever and inflammation remedy
Seeds as edible seed snack

commodities.name: Amla (Indian Gooseberry)
commodities.description: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is the richest natural source of vitamin C on earth - one small 100g amla contains 600-800 mg vitamin C, 20× the content of an orange - and is the foundational ingredient in Chyawanprash, India's most consumed Ayurvedic health supplement (₹2,000+ crore market). UP's Pratapgarh district is the amla capital of India and processes over 60% of national production.
uses: Amla powder for Chyawanprash and health supplements
Amla murabba (preserved amla in sugar)
Amla oil for hair strengthening (major cosmetics use)
Fresh amla juice (health tonic - vitamin C supplement)
Triphala churna (Ayurvedic digestive - amla is one of three fruits)

commodities.name: Jackfruit
commodities.description: India is the world's largest jackfruit producer and Kerala's Varikka and Koozha jackfruit varieties can weigh 35-50 kg per fruit, making jackfruit the world's largest tree-borne fruit. Raw jackfruit (kathal) is India's most popular meat substitute, and the ₹500+ crore packaged jackfruit product market (curries, vegan pulled-jack, chips) is growing at 25% annually as plant-based diets gain traction.
uses: Raw jackfruit curry (kathal sabzi - meat substitute)
Ripe jackfruit eating and pulp
Jackfruit chips (crispy snack - Kerala cottage industry)
Vegan pulled jackfruit export to USA, UK, Europe
Jackfruit seed curry and dal (tribal nutrition)

commodities.name: Custard Apple (Sitaphal)
commodities.description: Custard apple (sitaphal/sharifa) is India's most distinct tropical fruit and Maharashtra's Nashik, Dhule and Nanded districts have developed commercial cultivation earning farmers ₹1.5-3 lakh/acre. The cherimoya (hybrid custard apple) commands ₹150-300/kg retail in urban India and the processed pulp is used in ice cream, shakes and health drinks.
uses: Fresh eating (dessert fruit)
Custard apple ice cream and milkshake (commercial use)
Pulp extraction for health drinks
Seed oil for herbal cosmetics (hair oil)
Pest-control spray from seed extract (natural pesticide)

commodities.name: Peach (Aadoo)
commodities.description: India's Himalayan peach belt in Himachal Pradesh (Shimla, Kullu, Kinnaur), Uttarakhand and J&K produces the finest stone fruits in Asia but suffers from extreme post-harvest losses due to peach's 3-5 day shelf life. Peach jam, squash and juice processing units in HP are rapidly scaling up to convert this into shelf-stable products, and Kinnaur's organically grown peaches are premium-priced at ₹150-300/kg.
uses: Fresh eating (primary - very short shelf life)
Peach jam and preserve export
Dried peaches (Himachal cottage industry)
Peach juice and nectar manufacturing
Canned peach halves for export

commodities.name: Pear (Nashpati)
commodities.description: Himachal Pradesh produces 70% of India's pear (nashpati) and the Pathankot-Baijnath valley in Kangra district and Kinnaur are prime production zones. India imports significant quantities of pear from China and South Africa to meet demand during off-season, creating an opportunity for Indian growers willing to invest in cold-chain infrastructure to command higher prices.
uses: Fresh eating (primary use)
Pear jam and pickle export (HP cottage industry)
Canned pear in syrup for export
Pear juice for beverages
Dried pear slices for health snacks

commodities.name: Plum (Aloo Bukhara)
commodities.description: Himachal Pradesh's Shimla and Kullu valleys and J&K's Srinagar produce India's finest plums and prunes, with the Aloo Bukhara (Damson-type purple plum) being the most traded variety. Indian plums are increasingly being processed into prunes (dried plums) - with Kinnaur emerging as a prune-drying hub - for the growing prune export market in the UAE and Saudi Arabia.
uses: Fresh eating and seasonal fruit market
Aloo Bukhara (dried prune) export to Middle East
Plum jam and preserve
Plum wine and distilled arak (J&K)
Traditional remedy for constipation (prune)

commodities.name: Fig (Anjeer)
commodities.description: India's fig (anjeer) belt is concentrated in Maharashtra's Pune, Nasik and Solapur districts, where the BAIF-developed hybrid variety Poona Fig has become nationally popular. Fresh anjeer sells at ₹80-150/kg retail while dried anjeer commands ₹400-1,200/kg, and Iran's competition in the dried fig export market is a persistent challenge for Indian exporters.
varieties: Poona Fig (Maharashtra BAIF hybrid - most popular)
uses: Fresh fig eating (seasonal, high-value)
Dried anjeer for export and health food
Anjeer milk and sweetened fig paste (health tonic)
Fig jam and preserve
Pharmaceutical: natural laxative and digestive supplement

commodities.name: Jamun (Java Plum)
commodities.description: Jamun (java plum/black plum) is a uniquely Indian fruit with deep Ayurvedic significance - its seed powder is a widely prescribed remedy for type-2 diabetes management and jamun vinegar is one of India's oldest home medicines. Despite being a traditional backyard tree, commercial jamun cultivation in UP and Maharashtra is growing, with fresh jamun selling at ₹60-120/kg retail during May-July.
uses: Fresh eating (summer fruit)
Jamun juice for diabetes management (huge demand)
Jamun seed powder (pharmaceutical - anti-diabetic)
Jamun vinegar (Ayurvedic medicine)
Wine and fermented jamun sherbet (cottage industry)

commodities.name: Mulberry (Shahtoot)
commodities.description: India is the world's second-largest silk producer and Karnataka's Ramanagara district (formerly Silk City) processes 70% of India's mulberry silk cocoon production. Mulberry (shahtoot) cultivation is inseparable from sericulture - 9 million silkworm-rearing farmers across Karnataka, West Bengal and J&K depend on mulberry orchards for their primary income.
uses: Silkworm feed (primary commercial use)
Fresh mulberry fruit eating and jam
Mulberry leaf tea (health and Ayurveda)
Mulberry leaf extract for blood sugar management
Mulberry wood for sports goods and tools

commodities.name: Walnut (Akhrot)
commodities.description: Jammu & Kashmir produces 96% of India's walnuts and the Wular lake belt of Sopore-Baramulla and Shopian is the walnut epicentre - over 3 lakh farming families depend on walnut trees, many of which are 100+ years old. Kashmiri walnut commands a ₹30-80% premium over Iranian and US walnuts in Indian markets due to its paper-thin shell and buttery taste.
uses: Edible kernel - health snack and cooking ingredient
Walnut oil for food and cosmetics (premium)
Walnut wood for furniture and carvings (very high value)
Confectionery (walnut fudge, barfi)
Export of walnuts-in-shell to USA, Germany, UAE

commodities.name: Almond (Badam)
commodities.description: J&K's Budgam, Pulwama and Anantnag districts produce India's indigenous Mamra almond - a soft-shell variety richer in oil than California almonds - and these sell at ₹3,000-5,000/kg retail compared to ₹700-1,200/kg for imported Californian almonds. India imports 90% of its almond requirement from the USA (primarily), making domestic Mamra almond one of the most valuable tree crops per hectare.
varieties: Non Pareil (California type, trial in HP)
uses: Edible kernel - premium snack and health food
Almond oil for cooking and cosmetics
Almond milk and almond flour (health food trend)
Confectionery (kalakand, barfi, halwa)
Skin care and hair oil (almond oil massage)

commodities.name: Marigold (Genda Phool)
commodities.description: Marigold (genda phool) is India's most commercially grown flower crop - the vibrant orange garlands are essential in virtually every Hindu wedding, puja and festival, creating year-round demand. Karnataka is the top producer and India exports marigold extract (lutein and zeaxanthin from dried petals) to the USA and Europe for eye-health supplements at ₹1,500-3,000/kg.
uses: Wedding and puja decoration garlands
Loose flower sale for temple offerings
Lutein and zeaxanthin extraction for eye health supplements
Natural yellow/orange food and textile dye
Dried marigold petals for herbal tea and pot-pourri

commodities.name: Mentha (Pudina / Mint)
commodities.description: Uttar Pradesh produces 85-90% of India's mentha (mint) crop and India is the world's largest mentha oil producer, supplying 80% of global demand for natural menthol used in toothpastes, mouthwashes, confectionery, pharmaceutical throat lozenges and pan masala. UP's Barabanki, Badaun and Rampur districts are the world's mentha oil hub, with steam distillation units processing millions of tonnes annually.
uses: Menthol crystals for pharma (cough drops, balms)
Peppermint oil for toothpaste and mouthwash
Flavouring for confectionery (mint candy)
Pan masala and gutkha flavour ingredient
Aromatherapy and skincare products

commodities.name: Guar Seed (Cluster Bean Seed)
commodities.description: Guar seed is India's most strategically valuable industrial crop because guar gum controls 85% of the global fracking fluid thickener market - every oil well drilled in the USA and Canada requires guar gum. Rajasthan produces 70% of India's guar and the commodity price oscillates wildly with US shale oil drilling activity, making guar one of the most volatile commodity markets in India.
uses: Guar gum for oil drilling fracking fluid (US shale oil - biggest use)
Food-grade guar gum (E412) for ice cream, sauces, bakery
Textile sizing and paper manufacturing
Guar meal for cattle and poultry feed
Pharmaceutical tablet binder and stabiliser

commodities.name: Ashwagandha (Withania)
commodities.description: Ashwagandha (Indian ginseng) is India's fastest-growing medicinal crop and the global adaptogen supplement market for ashwagandha root extract (withanolide standardised) is growing at 15% annually, reaching ₹8,000+ crore. India exports 90% of global ashwagandha requirement, with Madhya Pradesh's Mandsaur and Neemuch - already India's opium trading hubs - now becoming major ashwagandha processing centres.
varieties: Local Rajasthan wild type (high potency but low yield)
uses: Withanolide extract for stress and anxiety supplements
Ashwagandha root powder for KSM-66 and Sensoril extracts (export)
Classical Ayurvedic rasayana (rejuvenator)
Fitness supplement - testosterone and recovery support
Animal tonic preparation in veterinary Ayurveda

commodities.name: Lemongrass (Cymbopogon)
commodities.description: India is the world's largest lemongrass oil producer and the Nilgiri foothills of Kerala and Odisha's Ganjam district supply most of India's high-quality citral-rich lemongrass oil to the global flavour, fragrance and pharmaceutical industries. Lemongrass oil (citral content 70-85%) is the primary raw material for synthesising ionone (violet perfume) and Vitamin A precursors in the chemical industry.
uses: Lemongrass essential oil for perfumery and cosmetics
Citral extraction for ionone (violet fragrance synthesis)
Vitamin A precursor manufacturing (pharmaceutical)
Lemongrass tea (health beverage)
Natural insect repellent and aromatherapy

commodities.name: Poppy Seed (Khus Khus)
commodities.season: Rabi (Sow: Oct-Nov, Harvest: Feb-Mar) - licensed crop
commodities.description: India is the world's only legal large-scale opium producer under International Narcotics Control Board (INCB) licence, cultivated in MP, HP and Rajasthan on strictly licensed plots. The poppy seed (khus khus) is the legal culinary byproduct and is a premium spice (zero alkaloid content in the seed) used in Mughal-origin gravies, bread and halwa, selling at ₹700-1,500/kg retail.
uses: Khus khus in cooking (creamy gravies, curries, halwa)
Poppy seed bread topping (export bakery)
Opium latex for pharmaceutical morphine and codeine (licensed)
Cold-pressed poppy seed oil for salads (Europe)
Bird feed ingredient (small quantity)

commodities.name: Bay Leaf (Tej Patta)
commodities.description: Indian bay leaf (tej patta) is the leaf of the Cinnamomum tamala tree - botanically distinct from European bay laurel (Laurus nobilis) - and gives a unique cinnamon-clove flavour that is irreplaceable in Indian biryani and garam masala. Uttarakhand's Tehri Garhwal and Chamoli districts supply most of India's tej patta from wild-harvested trees, and the leaves are exported to the USA and the UK at ₹8,000-15,000/quintal.
uses: Biryani and pulao flavouring (essential spice)
Garam masala blend ingredient
Bay leaf essential oil for perfumery
Export to USA, UK as whole dried spice
Traditional remedy for diabetes (research-backed)

commodities.name: Long Pepper (Pipali)
commodities.description: Long pepper (pipali) was the original pepper of the ancient world - more widely traded than black pepper in classical India and Rome - and is experiencing a revival as a premium Ayurvedic ingredient. It contains piperine at 4-5% (versus 2-4% in black pepper) and the bioavailability-enhancing property of piperine is driving pharmaceutical demand for pipali extract in nutraceutical formulations globally.
uses: Traditional Ayurvedic medicine for respiratory disorders
Trikatu formulation (pipali, black pepper, ginger)
Piperine extraction for pharmaceutical bioavailability
Export to USA, Germany for supplement manufacturing
Spice in pickles and traditional cooking
